label: Bonanza
terms_note: Apply for an API account at api.bonanza.com/accounts/new (dev_id + cert_id); each seller grants a user token through the fetchToken URL (valid about a year or until revoked); no rate limit and no fee published; no sandbox; large booths (>40k items) get asynchronous queued processing.

discovery.auth: token (dev_id + cert_id headers; per-seller user token via fetchToken URL flow, ~1-year lifetime)
sdks: official code samples .NET / Python / PHP / Java / Ruby / Perl on api.bonanza.com/docs

rate_limits: not published on the docs index

reference.verdict: **Verdict** — has_api: **yes**.Confidence: **high** — official developer documentation opened by the auditor.
auth: 1. Apply for an API account → dev_id and cert_id; send them as `X-BONANZLE-API-DEV-NAME` / `X-BONANZLE-API-CERT-NAME` headers.
2. Call fetchToken → returns a URL; the seller opens it, approves access on bonanza.com; the token is then returned (getTokenStatus).
3. Put the token in `requesterCredentials.bonanzleAuthToken` on every secure call; tokens live ~1 year or until the user deactivates them.

endpoints.notes: title ≤ 80 chars, description ≤ 60,000 chars HTML, price, quantity, up to 4 picture URLs or multipart, domestic + international shipping; response itemId, categoryId, sellingState

reference.limits: Not published on any page opened. - API account application (free); user tokens granted by each seller. - Pictures given by URL must be reachable by bonanza.com. - Booths with more than 40k items are processed asynchronously (queued response).
mcp_sdk: SDK: official code samples .NET / Python / PHP / Java / Ruby / Perl on api.bonanza.com/docs

fields.name: dev_id
fields.help: Developer id (dev_id) of your approved Bonanza API account (api.bonanza.com > Apply for an API account); sent as the X-BONANZLE-API-DEV-NAME header.

fields.name: cert_id
fields.help: Certificate id (cert_id) of the same API account; sent as the X-BONANZLE-API-CERT-NAME header.

fields.name: auth_token
fields.help: The seller's verified user token (fetchToken, then the seller approves it at the returned authentication URL); sent in every request body as requesterCredentials.bonanzleAuthToken. Tokens expire a year after issue or when the seller deactivates them.

adapter.terms: Bonapitit (Bonanza's API) takes one JSON object per call, {"<callName>Request": {...}}, POSTed to /api_requests/secure_request; the answer carries ack (Success|Failure|Warning) and <callName>Response.

me.note: getTokenStatus returns getTokenStatusResponse {verified, hardExpirationTime} for the configured seller token.

create_listing.note: addFixedPriceItem with allowForSale=true: the item is PUBLISHED for sale in the seller's booth immediately when it has every required field (sellingState Active). `price` is in US dollars; title at most 80 characters; up to 4 image URLs fetched by Bonanza. Category is guessed by Bonanza and no shipping is sent, so an item without a shipping setting comes back as 'Missing required fields' with the missing fields in raw.message. `currency` is not a field of the call.

end_listing.note: endFixedPriceItem removes the item from the seller's booth; endFixedPriceItemResponse.itemsRemoved (in raw) is the number actually removed (0 means nothing was ended).

list_orders.note: getOrders as seller: orderStatus (Active|Cancelled|Completed|Incomplete|InProcess|Invoiced|Proposed|Shipped; Completed = paid, not yet shipped), createTimeFrom (dateTime), entriesPerPage (max 100) and pageNumber (max 100). Each row is orderArray[].order; `total` is order.total (a decimal string, US dollars), items and shipping address in raw.

mark_shipped.note: completeSale {transactionID (= order id), shipped: true, shipment {shippingTrackingNumber, shippingCarrierUsed}} marks the order shipped. `carrier` must be one of usps, ups, fedex, other.

not_offered.update_listing: reviseFixedPriceItem documents only itemId and discardOldVariations as inputs (https://api.bonanza.com/docs/reference/revise_fixed_price_item); which item fields it accepts is not documented. Price/quantity changes go through updateInventory, whose body is keyed by the item id itself ('updates.itemId.price') — an object key built from an argument, which the declarative body cannot express.
not_offered.set_inventory: updateInventory takes 'updates.itemId.quantity', i.e. a JSON object whose KEY is the item id ({"updates": {"<itemId>": {"quantity": n}}}); the declarative body builds only fixed keys, and there is no SKU-addressed stock call.

evidence: host api.bonanza.com: DNS ok, TLSv1.3 (Google Trust Services)
probe: 5/5 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 301 (redirect), so the answers are path-specific
HTML docs spot-check (render-doc): 5/5 tool paths found verbatim on their docs pages; every parameter and body key named on the page
